## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

RaceDao — core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/RaceDao.kt

## Trigger

saveRecordedRace, in RaceRepositoryImpl (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt) — observed

## Today

`RaceRepositoryImpl.saveRecordedRace` calls `raceDao.findBySourceRaceId(raceId)`
and, when it returns null, later calls `persist(race, sourceRaceId = raceId)`,
which itself calls `raceDao.upsert(...)`. The lookup and the write are two
separate `RaceDao` calls with no `@Transaction` spanning both, and
`saveRecordedRace` holds no lock. `RaceDao.upsert` is itself `@Transaction`,
but only around delete-then-insert of one race's rows — it starts after the
lookup has already returned, so two concurrent calls to `saveRecordedRace`
with the same `raceId` can both pass the lookup before either writes.
`RaceEntity.sourceRaceId` (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/RaceEntity.kt)
carries no `@Index` and no uniqueness constraint — `findBySourceRaceId`'s
`WHERE sourceRaceId = :sourceRaceId` query is a full table scan, and
`RaceDao.insertRace` uses `OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE` keyed only on the
primary key `id`, so nothing at the schema level stops two rows from
sharing one `sourceRaceId`. `RaceDatabaseMigrations.MIGRATION_1_2`, which
added the `sourceRaceId` column, created no index either.

## Expected

The lookup and the write happen inside one `@Transaction` method on
`RaceDao` — a single `findOrInsertRecordedRace`-style entry point that
`RaceRepositoryImpl.saveRecordedRace` calls once, replacing its own
find-then-persist sequence, so no other caller can interleave a write
for the same `sourceRaceId` between the check and the insert.

A second, related gap: `RaceEntity.sourceRaceId` needs a unique index
(`@Index(value = ["sourceRaceId"], unique = true)`), and — because
Room schemas are exported and versioned (TECHNICAL_CONVENTIONS.md §8)
— a new migration creating that unique index on the existing `races`
table, alongside the schema version bump. Without it, the lookup
stays a full scan and the transaction alone does not stop two rows
from sharing one `sourceRaceId` if the insert path is ever reached
through a different route than the new transactional method.
